input: Source recycled glass tiles for the kitchen backsplash

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The total square footage of the backsplash area determines how much tile to source and directly affects cost and supplier minimums.
A hard budget ceiling rules out certain suppliers, premium product lines, or custom options entirely.
Recycled glass tiles vary widely in color, finish, size, and pattern — the aesthetic direction narrows the supplier shortlist dramatically.
Whether the user needs local pickup, will accept shipping, or requires a specific retailer type affects which sourcing channels are viable.
The project timeline (e.g., renovation already underway vs. planning phase) sets urgency and determines whether lead times from specialty suppliers are acceptable.
Knowing whether a professional installer is involved or this is DIY affects whether trade-only suppliers are accessible and what format guidance is needed.
The user may prioritise maximum recycled content, certifications (e.g., LEED), price, or aesthetics — the definition of the 'best' tile differs entirely based on this.

gold.taskTitle: Source recycled glass tiles for kitchen backsplash
gold.taskDescription: Find and procure recycled glass tiles suitable for installing as a kitchen backsplash.

questions.title: What is the total square footage of your backsplash area?
questions.description: Establish the exact area to be tiled so sourcing quantities and supplier minimums can be matched accurately.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the tiles themselves?
questions.description: Identify the hard spending limit to filter out product lines and suppliers that fall outside the affordable range.

questions.title: What colors, finishes, or tile sizes are you drawn to?
questions.description: Capture aesthetic preferences to narrow the shortlist of recycled glass tile styles and suppliers.

questions.title: Do you need a local supplier, or is online ordering acceptable?
questions.description: Determine viable sourcing channels — local tile showrooms, home improvement stores, or online specialty retailers.

questions.title: When do the tiles need to be ready for installation?
questions.description: Establish the deadline or urgency to judge whether standard lead times, in-stock items, or expedited options are required.

questions.title: Will a professional contractor be installing these tiles?
questions.description: Clarify whether trade-only suppliers and contractor accounts are accessible, or if sourcing must be consumer-facing.

questions.title: What matters most — recycled content percentage, eco-certifications, or price?
questions.description: Define the primary success criterion so the best tile can be identified when trade-offs between sustainability, credentials, and cost arise.
